title: Hard-delete endpoint (`DELETE /:evidenceId/hard`) has no retention period check, no immutability lock on approved/submitted evidence — two clicks permanently destroys certification evidence; violates A.5.33
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence.controller.js` — `hardDeleteEvidence` handler
**Root Cause:** The `DELETE /:evidenceId/hard` route calls the delete service with no pre-check on the evidence status or any retention policy. There is no immutability lock on evidence in `submitted`, `approved`, or `active` states. Any user with `evidence.delete` permission can permanently destroy certification evidence in two clicks with no grace period.
**Impact:** Direct violation of ISO 27001:2022 A.5.33. Evidence destroyed cannot be recovered; Stage 2 auditors will find unexplained gaps in the chain of custody.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
File: vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence.controller.js — hardDeleteEvidence handler

1. Before the delete call, look up the evidence record and check its `status`.
2. If status is `submitted`, `approved`, or `active`, return 400: "Active evidence cannot be hard-deleted — archive it first."
3. Add an `isImmutable` boolean field to the evidence schema; set it to true when status transitions to `approved`. Block delete if `isImmutable === true`.
4. Add a `RETENTION_PERIOD_DAYS` env var (default 2555 / 7 years). If `createdAt > now - retentionPeriod`, return 400: "Evidence is within the retention period and cannot be deleted."
5. Log every hard-delete attempt (success or rejection) to the audit trail with actor, timestamp, and reason.
```

title: Review decision comment has no minimum length — blank or single-character approval accepted in `EvidenceMyReviewsTab.jsx`; certification body would challenge approvals with no justification; violates ISO 19011:2018 §6.4.9
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/EvidenceMyReviewsTab.jsx` — `handleApprove`/`handleReject`; backend review endpoint
**Root Cause:** The approval and rejection submit handlers pass `reviewComment` to the API without any minimum-length validation. The Textarea has no `minLength` HTML attribute and no JS guard. The backend review endpoint does not validate comment length either. Every approved evidence item therefore has a legally challengeable audit trail under ISO 19011:2018 §6.4.9.
**Impact:** An entire evidence repository can have single-character approvals. A certification body reviewing approval justifications will raise a major nonconformity.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
File: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/EvidenceMyReviewsTab.jsx

1. In handleApprove and handleReject, add before the API call:
   if (!reviewComment || reviewComment.trim().length < 50) {
     setCommentError('Justification must be at least 50 characters');
     return;
   }
2. Pass `error={commentError}` and `helperText={commentError}` to the Textarea.
3. Clear the error on every keystroke: onChange={() => setCommentError(null)}.

File: backend evidence review endpoint (evidence.controller.js or evidenceReview.service.js)
4. Add server-side validation: reviewComment: Joi.string().min(50).required()
5. Return 422 with field-level error if validation fails.
```

title: Export/Share feature is a UI mockup — 'Generate Secure Link', 'Send via Email', 'Portal Access' cards have no click handlers or functional modals in `ExportShareContent.jsx`; presented as fully implemented; violates Clause 7.5.3
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/ExportShareContent.jsx`
**Root Cause:** The "Generate Secure Link", "Send via Email", and "Portal Access" action cards render with no `onClick` handlers and no backend routes exist for any of these operations. The feature was scaffolded as a UI mockup and never implemented. The `staticRecentExports` fallback array contains hardcoded entries dated 2025-12-28 that are presented as real export history.
**Impact:** The primary mechanism for delivering evidence packages to an external certification body does not function. Fabricated export history constitutes a document integrity violation under Clause 7.5 and A.5.36.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
This requires full implementation. Minimum viable path:

Backend — create two new routes:
1. POST /evidence/export/secure-link — generates a signed JWT URL granting time-limited read access to specified evidenceIds[]. Store the grant in MongoDB with expiresAt, createdBy, accessCount.
2. GET /evidence/export/history — returns real export records for the org (empty array on first use).

Frontend — ExportShareContent.jsx:
3. Delete the `staticRecentExports` array entirely.
4. Replace with <EmptyState title="No exports yet" /> when history is empty.
5. Wire "Generate Secure Link" onClick to open a modal: evidence multi-select, expiry picker (7/30/90 days), optional password. On submit call the backend, display the generated URL with a copy button.
6. Mark "Send via Email" and "Portal Access" with <Badge>Coming soon</Badge> and disabled={true} until implemented.
```
